definitions.explanation: A music genre originating in African American communities, characterized by improvisation, syncopated rhythms, and brass/woodwind instruments.

examples.japanese: ジャズを{聴|き}きながらコーヒーを{飲|の}む。
examples.english: I drink coffee while listening to jazz.

examples.japanese: ジャズの{生|なま}{演奏|えんそう}を{楽|たの}しんだ。
examples.english: I enjoyed a live jazz performance.

examples.japanese: ジャズピアノを{習|なら}っている。

notes:
ジャズ refers to jazz music. Japan has a strong jazz culture, with many live venues, festivals, and a dedicated listener community.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ジャズを{聴|き}く (to listen to jazz)
- ジャズを{演奏|えんそう}する (to play jazz)
- ジャズバー / ジャズクラブ (jazz bar / jazz club)
- ジャズフェスティバル (jazz festival)
- ジャズピアニスト (jazz pianist)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan has been one of the world's largest markets for jazz since the mid-20th century. ジャズ{喫茶|きっさ} (jazz cafés where patrons listen to records) are a distinctly Japanese institution.

SUBGENRES:
- ビバップ (bebop)
- スウィング (swing)
- フュージョン (fusion)
- フリージャズ (free jazz)
